artworks.title: Theseus Slaying the Minotaur (tondo of the Aison Kylix)
artworks.description: In the central tondo of this Attic red-figure drinking cup, the Athenian hero Theseus drags the slain Minotaur from the heart of the Cretan Labyrinth while the goddess Athena, his divine protectress, stands by in attendance. Signed by the painter Aison and dated to the late Classical period (c. 435-415 BC), the cup distills the most famous of Theseus's exploits into a single charged moment of triumph. Standing 14.2 cm high with a diameter of 36.4 cm, it survives among the masterworks of Athenian vase painting and is today held in the Museo Arqueologico Nacional in Madrid (inv. 11365).

artworks.title: Theseus Victorious over the Minotaur
artworks.description: This Roman fresco from the House of M. Gavius Rufus at Pompeii (region VII, 2, 16) shows Theseus standing in calm heroic nudity over the crumpled body of the Minotaur, as the freed Athenian youths and maidens crowd forward to grasp his hands and Cretans approach in wonder. Painted in the Fourth Pompeian Style and measuring 97 by 88 cm, the panel translates the Greek legend into the idiom of imperial Roman domestic decoration. Recovered from the buried city, it is now preserved in the Museo Archeologico Nazionale di Napoli (inv. 9043).

artworks.title: Theseus Defeats the Centaur
artworks.description: Antonio Canova's monumental marble group captures Theseus astride a vanquished centaur, his fist raised to deliver the killing blow at the wedding battle of the Lapiths and Centaurs, where the hero fought alongside his friend Pirithous. Carved between 1805 and 1819 and standing some 340 cm high, the Neoclassical colossus was first commissioned by Napoleon for Milan before being acquired by Emperor Franz I of Austria. It now presides over the grand staircase of the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna, an emblem of order triumphing over savagery.

artworks.title: Theseus Slaying the Minotaur
artworks.description: The French Romantic sculptor Antoine-Louis Barye, celebrated as a master of animal anatomy, cast this dramatic bronze of Theseus wrestling the bull-headed Minotaur to the ground, the hero's body coiled in muscular tension as he forces his monstrous adversary down. Modeled in 1843, the work fuses Barye's naturalistic vigor with the heroic grandeur of myth. It is held in the collection of the Baltimore Museum of Art.
